name: StructMemEval
ontology_notes: Eval of memory organization in LLM agents, not a memory engine. User modeled is a notepad-augmented agent handling ledgers, family trees, corporate graphs, location/state machines, and preference statistics from event history. 207 scenarios (90 tree, 45 count, 42 state, 30 recommendation) and over 2,000 questions. Main set is 51 longest problems (10 tree, 15 count, 14 state, 12 recsys), each at least 250 messages. Metric is gpt-4o-mini judge accuracy against a reference answer. Steal organization metrics. Failure modes named in the paper are incorrect structures, memory hallucinations, and record duplication. Still not RP. Misses hole 1 identity drift after 50-plus sessions, hole 2 socially wrong timing, hole 3 joke stored as relationship fact, hole 4 user retcon vs character lie vs narrator, hole 5 cross-character leak, hole 6 lorebook treated as lived event, hole 7 poisoned memory overrides system persona, hole 8 cost per turn, hole 9 forget-that, hole 10 three-month reunion.

supersession.evidence: State-tracking scenarios change entity state over transitions (move cities, neighbors, kanban). Count-based tasks net later transactions against earlier ones. That is structured overwrite of a ledger or location, not a biographical fact-replacement category.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: State tracking is ordered by number of transitions. Questions are asked at different conversation depths. No dated 'last Tuesday' queries and no months-apart reunion.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: Synthetic trees, settlements, locations, and media preferences. No user vs character vs relationship vs lore types. README case files use a single benchmark user_id.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: No abstention, trauma, kink, spoiler, or social-timing items. Optional memory-organization hints tell the agent how a human would structure the ledger. They are analysis-only.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Hallucination and record duplication are failure modes of the agent under test. They are not stored-text jailbreaks or persona overwrite probes.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No user 'forget that' items. State changes keep the latest location or netted total. They do not delete a stored fact on request.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Reported number is accuracy vs problem size (edges, transitions, transactions). Limitations mention API cost of long encodings. No tokens-per-turn meter.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Apache-2.0 LICENSE on GitHub. README requires OPENAI_API_KEY for the mem0 embedder (text-embedding-3-large). Judge is gpt-4o-mini. Open-weight backbones appear in Table 2 (deepseek-v4-flash/pro).
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Would prefer systems that keep a graph, ledger, or running statistic instead of dumping top-k snippets. Steal those organization metrics. It would not select for RP identity, silence, poisoning, or forget-that.

published_eval.name: StructMemEval
published_eval.claimed_score: Paper Table 1, gemini-3.1-pro backbone, main set. mem-agent total 0.55 (state 0.84, tree 0.98, count 0.00, recsys 0.37). Retrieval 0.06. Mem0 0.30. EMem 0.25. Count-based column is 0.00 for every listed agent. Table 2 mem-agent totals range 0.27 (claude-opus-4.7) to 0.55 (gemini-3.1-pro).
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Whether an agent organizes long synthetic histories into structures a human notepad would keep (graphs, nets, state machines, preference aggregates) and then answers later questions. Judge is gpt-4o-mini factual correctness. Not companion identity, silence, or poisoning.

open_unknowns: Paper introduction says the main set of 51 scenarios and at least 200 additional tasks. Later it says 207 scenarios total. Using 51 main plus 207 extended.
README describes the paper as work in progress. Using the arXiv v3 extract as the paper source.
